identification.summary: UNC2970 is Mandiant's designation for a suspected North Korean cyber espionage cluster, tracked since 2021 and first described publicly in March 2023 [S1][S3]. It is known for job-recruitment spear-phishing in which fake recruiter personas (including fake LinkedIn accounts impersonating real people) move targets to WhatsApp or email and deliver malware [S1][S3]. Mandiant suspects with high confidence that it is UNC577 (TEMP.Hermit) [S1].
identification.firstObserved: Mandiant describes UNC2970 as tracked since 2021 [S3]. Its March 2023 report describes activity observed from June 2022, including a campaign against a U.S. technology company [S1].
identification.notes: Mandiant merged the earlier cluster UNC4034 (WhatsApp-based DPRK phishing in 2022) into UNC2970 [S1][S3]. Mandiant notes multiple overlaps with the publicly reported Operation Dream Job and a similar WhatsApp approach in a 2022 Microsoft (ZINC) report [S1]. Mandiant also states it saw shared code and tooling patterns (such as compromised WordPress C2) across other DPRK groups, and did not mention Lazarus Group in the LIGHTSHOW report [S1]. Secondary press equates TEMP.Hermit with Lazarus Group or Diamond Sleet [S5]; that mapping is not stated in the Mandiant pages fetched and is not adopted here. No Microsoft actor name was verified in this pass.

attribution.sponsor: Mandiant describes UNC2970 as a suspected North Korean (DPRK) espionage group and as having a North Korea nexus [S1][S3]. No government attribution was found in the sources gathered.
attribution.confidence: Mandiant: suspected North Korean espionage group; suspected with high confidence to be UNC577 / TEMP.Hermit, based on technical indicators and TTPs [S1]. In 2024 Mandiant described it as suspected to have a North Korea nexus [S3]. Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) described it as North Korea-linked in 2026 coverage [S4][S6].
attribution.basis: Mandiant incident response and Managed Defense observations, infrastructure, tooling and TTP overlaps with UNC577/TEMP.Hermit [S1][S3].

objectives: Cyber espionage. Mandiant's 2024 report assesses that senior and manager-level targets in energy and aerospace were likely chosen for access to sensitive information [S3]. 2026 coverage of a GTIG report says the group profiled high-value defense and cybersecurity targets and technical job roles to support tailored recruiter personas [S4][S6].

regions: United States and Europe (2022 media and technology targeting) [S1]
United States, United Kingdom, Netherlands, Cyprus, Sweden, Germany, Singapore, Hong Kong, Australia (2024 campaign) [S3]
targeting.notes: 2022: Western media and technology companies, and security researchers at a U.S. technology company [S1]. 2024: senior and manager-level employees in energy and aerospace [S3]. Mandiant says its targeting of security researchers may indicate a shift or expansion in the group's activity [S1][S2]. 2026: press coverage of a GTIG report describes reconnaissance on cybersecurity and defense companies [S4][S6].

capabilities.summary: Initial access is job-themed social engineering: fake recruiter personas, Word documents using remote template injection, ZIP/ISO archives disguised as skills assessments, and in 2024 password-protected ZIPs with an encrypted PDF opened only through a trojanized SumatraPDF [S1][S3]. 2022-2023 tooling included the PLANKWALK DLL-sideloading backdoor, TOUCHMOVE, SIDESHOW (HTTP backdoor with at least 49 commands), TOUCHSHIFT, TOUCHSHOT, TOUCHKEY, HOOKSHOT, LIDSHIFT, LIDSHOT and CLOUDBURST [S1]. Compromised WordPress sites were the main C2 for template injection and malware [S1]. Mandiant observed push of malicious PowerShell through compromised accounts and Microsoft Intune, and a bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver (BYOVD) utility, LIGHTSHOW, that used Dell DBUtil 2.3 and ENE Technology drivers to patch kernel routines used by EDR products; a related vulnerable driver was assigned CVE-2022-42455 [S1][S2]. LIGHTSHOW was VMProtect-packed and host-keyed to resist analysis [S2]. In 2024 the chain was BURNBOOK (trojanized SumatraPDF libmupdf.dll), TEARPAGE (DLL search-order hijack loader) and MISTPEN (backdoor built on a trojanized Notepad++ binhex plugin); a later MISTPEN variant used Microsoft Graph/OneDrive for C2, and an earlier one used compromised WordPress sites [S3]. In 2026, press coverage of a GTIG report says the group used Gemini to profile targets [S4][S6].

campaigns.name: Campaign against Western media and technology companies; security researchers
campaigns.summary: Mandiant observed job-recruitment phishing, fake recruiter LinkedIn accounts and WhatsApp delivery against U.S. and European media and technology organizations, including a U.S. technology company where security researchers were suspected targets. Mandiant also reported abuse of Intune to deploy CLOUDBURST and the LIGHTSHOW BYOVD EDR-evasion tool.

campaigns.name: Mandiant publishes 'Stealing the LIGHTSHOW' Parts One and Two
campaigns.summary: Mandiant publicly designates UNC2970, merges UNC4034 into it, links it with high confidence to UNC577/TEMP.Hermit, and details PLANKWALK, the TOUCH* family, LIGHTSHIFT/LIGHTSHOW and the CVE-2022-42455 driver finding.

campaigns.name: Energy and aerospace job-lure campaign (BURNBOOK, TEARPAGE, MISTPEN)
campaigns.summary: Mandiant Managed Defense identified the activity in June 2024: recruiter pretexts delivered via WhatsApp and email with a password-protected ZIP containing an encrypted PDF and trojanized SumatraPDF, targeting senior-level staff in U.S. critical infrastructure verticals across nine countries. Published 2024-09-17.

campaigns.name: GTIG reports Gemini use for reconnaissance
campaigns.summary: Press coverage of a Google Threat Intelligence Group report says UNC2970 used Gemini to profile high-value targets, search for information on cybersecurity and defense companies, and map technical job roles and salary information. Primary GTIG text was not opened.

diamond.adversary: Suspected DPRK espionage cluster, high-confidence overlap with UNC577/TEMP.Hermit [S1][S3].
diamond.capability: Job-lure social engineering; PLANKWALK, SIDESHOW, MISTPEN and related malware; DLL sideloading; Intune abuse; BYOVD EDR evasion [S1][S2][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Compromised WordPress sites (including small-business sites in Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and South Africa), a compromised university SharePoint domain, and Microsoft Graph/OneDrive for later MISTPEN C2; WhatsApp and LinkedIn for victim contact [S1][S3].
diamond.victim: Media, technology, defense, energy and aerospace staff and security researchers in the U.S., Europe and Asia-Pacific [S1][S3].
diamond.socioPolitical: Espionage collection from sensitive sectors; no stated state tasking in the sources gathered [S3].
diamond.technology: Reliance on third-party messaging and social platforms (LinkedIn, WhatsApp), cloud management (Intune), cloud APIs (Microsoft Graph) and vulnerable signed drivers [S1][S2][S3].

gaps: Mandiant/GTIG ties to the Reconnaissance General Bureau were mentioned only in secondary search summaries; the Mandiant 2024 page fetched does not state RGB, so no RGB sponsor is asserted [S3].
Mapping of UNC2970/TEMP.Hermit to Lazarus Group and Microsoft's Diamond Sleet appears only in secondary press [S5]; Microsoft's name for this cluster was not verified, and MITRE group ID is unknown.

The primary GTIG February 2026 report was not opened; Gemini-use details rely on press coverage [S4][S6]. Press reports of the BYOVD and EDR focus beyond the 2023 Mandiant posts were not confirmed from a primary source.
Activity between 2024-09 and 2026-02, and any 2026 intrusions or victims, were not found.
Overlap with Operation Dream Job and UNC4034 is stated by Mandiant but the boundaries with other Dream Job clusters are not resolved [S1].
Several press sites (The Hacker News, The Record, Security Boulevard) could not be fetched; their detail is from search snippets only.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is personnel with professional social-media and messaging exposure (LinkedIn, WhatsApp), cloud management planes (Intune, Microsoft Graph tenants) and endpoint security tooling [S1][S3]. STEP 2: Defense and aerospace staff, energy sector managers and security researchers are the observed victim set; the actor adapts lures to a target's profile [S1][S3]. STEP 3: Template is recruiter contact, move to WhatsApp or email, archive with trojanized benign software, DLL sideloading, then C2 over compromised WordPress or Microsoft Graph, with BYOVD to blind EDR [S1][S2][S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued job-themed targeting of defense, aerospace, energy and security-research staff for espionage collection. MDCOA is targeting cleared or DIB personnel with tailored personas, using cloud identity abuse to reach networks without a VPN [S1][S3][S4]. Candidate indicators: unsolicited recruiter outreach followed by password-protected ZIP files; SumatraPDF or Notepad++ plugins running from user directories; scheduled task named 'Sumatra Launcher'; driver loads of DBUtil 2.3 or ENE drivers; Intune scripts from unexpected accounts; Graph API traffic from PDF readers [S1][S2][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: share the Mandiant indicators and recruiter-lure patterns with component cyber and counterintelligence teams, and track GTIG reporting for updates [S3][S6]. (2) Authorities: personal social media and messaging accounts are outside most DoD network authorities, so awareness training and CI reporting channels carry the response; coordinate with DC3 and the DIB program for contractors. (3) Mission assurance: enforce vulnerable-driver block rules and monitor EDR tamper events, since the actor targets EDR from kernel level [S2]. (4) Coordination: security researchers and red-team staff are a stated target set, so notify them through CI and insider-threat channels [S1].

provenance.importedSummary: UNC2970 is a North Korean threat actor that primarily targets organizations through spear-phishing emails with job recruitment themes, often utilizing fake LinkedIn accounts to engage victims. The group employs the PLANKWALK backdoor and other malware families, leveraging compromised WordPress sites for command and control. They have been observed using BYOVD techniques to exploit vulnerable drivers for evading detection. Mandiant has noted a shift in UNC2970's targeting strategy, including a focus on security researchers and advancements in their operational capabilities against EDR tools.
